$comment: Each entry breaks the product in one specific way and names the suite that must notice.
`node tools/ci/mutate.mjs` applies each in turn and reports any that SURVIVED - a mutation
nothing caught is a hole in the suite, stated as a fact rather than as an opinion.
WHY THIS EXISTS. Every defect worth finding in this repository has been the same shape: a test
that passes for the wrong reason. A reducer arm with no dispatcher. A gate whose regex required
an invisible control byte. Three tests that grepped source for a string that survived deleting
the wiring. Each was found by a person or a model READING, which is expensive and does not stay
found. A mutant is cheap and stays.
EVERY ENTRY BELOW LOCKS A REAL FIX. Nothing here is hypothetical - each `find` string is the
actual line some defect was closed with, so a refactor that quietly undoes one is caught by the
mutant that can no longer be killed.
ANALYZER MUTANTS TARGET `dist`, NOT `src`, and that is deliberate: its suite runs from dist, so
mutating source would need a 60-second rebuild per mutant. The question asked is 'does the
suite notice this behaviour change', and dist is where the behaviour is. `tools/ci/
mutants.test.mjs` separately proves every `find` string still exists, so a mutant that has
silently stopped applying cannot sit here looking useful.

AN EQUIVALENT MUTANT IS NOT A FINDING. The first version of the two keyless mutants below changed `let keylessLoopback = false` to `true` - and the next three lines overwrite it unconditionally, so the product behaved identically and the mutant 'survived' while proving nothing. Both now target the ASSIGNMENT. Before filing a survivor as a hole, reproduce it by hand and confirm the product actually misbehaves; the harness reports suspects, not verdicts.

BLANKING THE COMMENT TEXT TURNED OUT TO BE REDUNDANT. A mutant that stopped `lexicalView` overwriting comment characters with spaces could not be killed - because the `code` array, not the blanked text, is what excludes a match. Both belts are real, but only one is load-bearing, and the mutants now name the load-bearing one. Finding this took reproducing the survivor by hand; a survivor is a question, not an answer.

mutants.why: A rebound page could replace the AI provider and read the repository. The gate must run before routing, auth and any provider call.
/archgraph.json carries private repository topology and predates the /api namespace, so it is easy to forget.
A keyless provider config is only safe on loopback. A private-LAN address is still another machine and a wider disclosure boundary for repository context.
A proposed node wearing a scan citation is indistinguishable from something the scanner found - the exact fabrication this product exists to detect.

mutants.find: ` (stopped after ${maxResults} matches - there may be more; narrow the query or use a glob)`
mutants.why: Search capped at 20 and reported '20 matches'. Absence must be reported as a state, never as a clean bill of health.
The probe URLs are loopback literals, but following a redirect leaves localhost entirely.

Three agents defeated an earlier version of this gate by writing the construction in a // comment: the scanner saw it, the baseline row could be retired, and the feature stayed unreachable. Disabling this branch restores exactly that hole.

An import resolving EXACTLY to the deleted packages/web directory escaped a startsWith with an appended separator. This mutates a test helper on purpose: the thing being checked is that the guard test for the exact-directory case still exists.
Backspace inside the note editor bubbled to the board listener and deleted the whole note on the first keystroke.
A drag released outside the canvas never committed the move and left the drag stale.
A proposed id colliding with a scanned one drew the grounded, evidence-bearing node as a dashed ghost.

The start and list routes are one character apart and the client calls both. The call became multi-line when run budgets (timeoutMs/maxSteps) were added, so the find spans the route plus the opening of its body to name exactly one site.
Using a detected local model must actually fill the form it claims to fill; the first version of this feature could never be saved at all.

The keyless rule is enforced twice - once when a config is validated and again when a provider call is built. Validation can be bypassed by a config that was stored before the rule existed, so the call path needs its own mutant.
The brand firewall first caught only quoted px sizes, so a bare numeric fontSize: 14 in an inline style walked straight through the one gate that owns type scale.
The same attack in /* */ form. A lexer with two comment states needs two mutants, or half of it is guarded by nothing.
The third lexer state. A route or action name mentioned inside a documentation string must not count as wiring, or prose about a feature retires the row that tracks building it.
A board of unlabelled strokes is not a brief. Offering to send it produces a request whose entire content is that the reader drew twelve lines, and spends a metered turn to say so.

mutants.find: lines.push('This is from a whiteboard sketch, not from the scan — nothing on it is evidence.');
mutants.why: Grounded-not-guessed is the product's first non-negotiable. A sketch arriving without that sentence is indistinguishable, to the model, from something the scanner found.
Silence about the unlabelled marks lets the reader believe the assistant is looking at their diagram. The count is the one thing standing between a sketch and that misunderstanding.

Counting a file the glob EXCLUDED spends the examine budget on work never done, so the walk stops in the same place however narrow the glob is - and 'narrow with a glob', the advice the truncation message gives, becomes inert. Inert advice is worse than none: the reader follows it, gets the identical answer, and concludes the symbol is not in their repository.

A tab opened before a repository was attached kept saying 'no repo attached' while the engine answered from that repository's graph - and because ai-config is fetched gated on attachment, the model label never loaded either. Three reported symptoms, one staleness.

Treating a failed probe as staleness turns a flaky network into a boot loop: every focus re-runs the ladder, which fails, which marks it stale again. 'The engine stopped answering' has its own surface and is not this one.

The re-ask is tied to the moment a reader is about to believe what is on screen. Firing it for a hidden tab makes it a background poll, which is the thing PlatformReport's contract says this is not: a fact with a timestamp, not a status light.

The original defect exactly: the prompt asked for the one construct proseBlocks.ts refuses on purpose, and the reader got literal bullet characters. Re-adding it three lines above the format clause is how it would come back, so the test asserts the ABSENCE, not just the presence of the fix.

Two ask paths render into the same transcript. A formatting rule that covers only one of them leaves the other free to emit markdown nothing will render - which is the half the owner hit, since 'design me a system' takes the design path.

The guard's own comment says refusal exists so the MODEL can repair the call. Refusing without naming a single real id leaves it guessing the same invented endpoint again, and half a proposal is discarded before it can reach the board.

A slash mid-sentence is a path separator far more often than a command, and this product's questions are full of paths like packages/web2/src. An unanchored query opens the menu on every one of them and fights the reader continuously.
Without this the product advertises / in its most-read line and then posts '/plan' to the model as a question. An affordance that is named and then ignored is worse than one that was never offered.

v1 shipped three competing + menus and item 2.7 names that as a defect - three lists is three answers to 'what can I do here'. A slash registry that stops deriving from TOOLBELT becomes the fourth, and drifts the moment anyone edits either one.

A gate that collects nothing reports nothing missing and passes forever. This one found three real defects on its first run - two var(--r-6) radii on a scale the book says has six steps and only six, and a letter-spacing naming a --ls-* token that does not exist anywhere - all of which had been silently resolving to nothing.

The second loopback probe needs its own lock, and its ambiguity with the first is how it announced itself: adding it made the models-probe mutant match two sites, and the catalogue's applies-exactly-once gate refused the whole run rather than silently judging the wrong one.

Only Ollama reports a context length. A ring is a fraction, so drawing one with no denominator means inventing the denominator - and a plausible default like 128k is the confident wrong number CANON law 4 forbids, on the very surface whose usage line already says 'never invent a number'.
A turn can exceed the window; the provider truncates and says so elsewhere. An arc drawn at 140% laps itself and reads as 40% - the opposite of the truth, at the moment the reader most needs it.
